work.title: Five Children and It
work.note: Five Children and It é um romance infantil da inglesa E. Nesbit sobre cinco irmãos que encontram uma criatura mágica num buraco de areia e ganham um desejo por dia. A referência é a história de crianças que apresentam amigos e a criatura que encontram: This is….

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Americans say “mom” and the British say “mum”.
items.why: It is a classic difference between American and British English.

items.s: Mother’s Day in the USA is in May.
items.why: It is the second Sunday of May, the same as in Brazil.

items.s: Father’s Day is on the same date in the USA and Brazil.
items.why: In the USA it is in June (third Sunday). In Brazil it is in August.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 2/2

items.s: Minneapolis is known as the “City of Lakes”.
items.why: There are many lakes inside the city of Minneapolis, in Minnesota.

items.s: In English, “family” means only mother, father and children.
items.why: It can include grandparents, cousins, aunts and uncles too.

pages.instruction: Mais uma rodada: decida e explique.

pages.title: My family in Minneapolis · 1/3
paragraphs: My name is Greta, and I live in Minneapolis, Minnesota. People call my city the “City of Lakes”. Today I want to introduce my **family**.

“**This is my mother** and **my father**,” I tell my new friend Jordan. “**That’s my brother**. **His name is Leo.**” Leo is a student. He plays the guitar. Jordan asks, “**Do you have sisters?**” “**Yes, I have one sister**,” I say. “**She’s a nurse.**” My grandma is also in the photo. She is my best friend.
pages.prompt: Onde começa e o que acontece?

pages.title: My family in Minneapolis · 2/3
paragraphs: Jordan smiles. “**Your family is nice!**” “**Thank you!** Do you have a big family?” I ask. “Yes,” says Jordan, “and we always eat together.” Then he says, “**Come to dinner on Sunday!**” I answer, “**I’d love to!**”

I like to think about a book from 1902. The English writer E. Nesbit wrote “Five Children and It”. Five brothers and sisters find a magic creature in a sand pit. It gives them one wish every day. The children say, “**This is my sister! This is the baby!**” They love each other, but they also argue.

pages.title: My family in Minneapolis · 3/3
paragraphs: My family is like that book. We are not magic, but we laugh and argue. Family is the place where we learn to say, “This is my…” with love.
